nodes.label: H3 · Consumer Surveillance

nodes.label: 7Q10
nodes.desc: The lowest 7-consecutive-day average streamflow expected on average once every ten years — the design low flow for sizing effluent dilution.

nodes.label: AEP
nodes.desc: The investor-owned utility whose Ohio operating company serves much of the grid footprint in this record.

nodes.label: Assimilative capacity
nodes.desc: A stream's ability to dilute or assimilate an added load (or a loss of flow) without breaching water-quality criteria, evaluated at design low flow.

nodes.label: Behind-the-meter
nodes.desc: On-site generation that serves a load directly, without that power crossing the utility meter or the public grid.

nodes.label: Brownfield
nodes.desc: A property whose redevelopment is complicated by real or perceived contamination, often carrying cleanup obligations and dedicated funding.

nodes.label: CERCLA
nodes.desc: The federal Superfund statute governing the cleanup of contaminated sites and the strict, retroactive liability of the parties responsible for them.

nodes.label: CGP
nodes.desc: The NPDES general permit that authorizes stormwater discharges from construction sites disturbing an acre or more — including smaller sites within a common plan of development or sale that reaches an acre — under a standard set of conditions.

nodes.label: Closed-loop cooling
nodes.desc: A recirculating cooling design whose water loss is chiefly evaporation and blowdown, so it withdraws little but consumes most of what it takes.

nodes.label: CMAR
nodes.desc: A project-delivery method in which the construction manager joins during design and commits to a guaranteed maximum price for the build.

nodes.label: Colocation
nodes.desc: A data center that leases space, power, and cooling to multiple tenants who install their own hardware — distinct from a single operator's owned campus.

nodes.label: Common-control plumbing
nodes.desc: Shared registered agents, organizers, or addresses across entities — evidence of common administrative control, not of beneficial ownership.

nodes.label: Conditional use
nodes.desc: A use allowed in a zoning district only by case-by-case approval, granted with conditions rather than by right.

nodes.label: Consent decree
nodes.desc: A court-approved settlement in which a party agrees to specified actions under continuing judicial oversight, carrying the force of a court order.

nodes.label: Constructive denial
nodes.desc: An agency's failure to produce public records within a reasonable time, treated in law as a denial even though no formal refusal was issued.

nodes.label: Consumptive cooling
nodes.desc: Cooling water that is withdrawn and lost (mostly to evaporation) rather than returned to the source, reducing downstream flow.

nodes.label: CRA
nodes.desc: An Ohio property-tax-abatement district (R.C. 3735) that lets a municipality exempt the value of new construction to incentivize development.

nodes.label: Curve number
nodes.desc: The NRCS coefficient (0–100) relating land cover and soil to the depth of runoff a storm produces — the core parameter of the curve-number runoff method.

nodes.label: Dilution
nodes.desc: The clean receiving-water flow available to dilute a discharged load, sized at design low flow — the physical basis of a water-quality-based effluent limit.

nodes.label: Dissolved oxygen
nodes.desc: The oxygen dissolved in water and available to aquatic life; a core water-quality criterion that a discharge must not depress below standard.

nodes.label: DMR
nodes.desc: The self-reported effluent-monitoring data a permittee files with the regulator, the primary public record of whether a discharge meets its permit.

nodes.label: ECHO
nodes.desc: EPA's public database of facility permits, inspections, violations, and enforcement actions across its major programs.

nodes.label: Effluent
nodes.desc: Treated wastewater discharged to a receiving water; its pollutant concentrations and loads are capped by limits written into the NPDES permit.

nodes.label: EIA
nodes.desc: The federal statistical agency for U.S. energy production, consumption, and prices, and a primary source of utility-level demand data.

nodes.label: Enterprise zone
nodes.desc: An Ohio program that grants property-tax exemptions on new investment in a designated area in exchange for job-creation and investment commitments.

nodes.label: EPA
nodes.desc: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency — the federal environmental regulator that sets national standards and delegates much of their enforcement to states.

nodes.label: ESC
nodes.desc: The construction practices that keep disturbed soil and sediment out of stormwater and receiving waters while a site is being built.

nodes.label: FERC
nodes.desc: The federal regulator of interstate electricity transmission, wholesale power markets, and the RTOs that operate them.

nodes.label: FFA
nodes.desc: A CERCLA cleanup agreement between EPA and a federal facility that sets the enforceable schedule and terms for remediating a listed site.

nodes.label: Grant-refund clause
nodes.desc: RDA §5.5 — public grant awards (State 629 / ODOD Jobs & Commerce) can backfill and refund the developer's "private" road-work contribution, dollar for dollar.

nodes.label: HB
nodes.desc: A bill originating in the Ohio House of Representatives, cited by number where it changes the siting, tax, or environmental law a project turns on.

nodes.label: Heat reuse
nodes.desc: Capturing a data center's rejected thermal energy and redirecting it to on-site or district heating instead of dumping it — a cooling-design axis distinct from how much water the cooling draw consumes.

nodes.label: HSG
nodes.desc: The NRCS A–D classification of a soil by how readily it infiltrates water — a primary input to runoff curve-number modeling.

nodes.label: HUC
nodes.desc: The USGS nested numeric code that keys a hydrologic area at a chosen scale, from large subbasins (HUC-8) down to local subwatersheds (HUC-12).

nodes.label: Hyperscale data center
nodes.desc: A very large, cloud-scale data center campus; the local zoning code defines the term and gates it as a conditional use.

nodes.label: Hyperscaler
nodes.desc: A cloud operator that builds and runs data centers at massive scale — the class of companies (AWS, Microsoft, Google, Meta) behind most large campus projects.

nodes.label: IL6
nodes.desc: The U.S. Department of Defense cloud security classification for classified (SECRET-level) workloads — the tier that dictates a data center's physical and personnel controls.

nodes.label: Interconnection queue
nodes.desc: The backlog of proposed generators and large loads awaiting the grid-connection studies and approvals an RTO requires before they can energize.

nodes.label: JEDD
nodes.desc: An Ohio township–municipality compact (R.C. 715.70) that shares income-tax revenue from a development area without annexation.

nodes.label: Moratorium
nodes.desc: A temporary local ban on approving a class of development while a government reconsiders the rules that govern it.

nodes.label: NDA
nodes.desc: A confidentiality agreement that binds a party to secrecy, often shielding the terms and identity behind a data-center deal during site selection.

nodes.label: NPDES
nodes.desc: The Clean Water Act permit program that sets and enforces pollutant limits on point-source discharges to surface water.

nodes.label: NWIS
nodes.desc: The USGS system that serves real-time and historical streamflow and water-quality data from the national gauge network.

nodes.label: OEPA
nodes.desc: The Ohio Environmental Protection Agency — the state permitting and enforcement authority for water, air, and waste under delegated federal programs.

nodes.label: Once-through cooling
nodes.desc: A cooling design that withdraws water, passes it once to absorb heat, and returns nearly all of it to the source — warmer but not consumed.

nodes.label: OPC
nodes.desc: A design-phase cost estimate for a public project — the engineer's structured projection of what construction will cost, and the artifact this platform reconstructs from source PDFs.

nodes.label: OPSB
nodes.desc: The Ohio board that reviews and certifies the siting of major electric generation and transmission facilities.

nodes.label: ORC
nodes.desc: The codified statutes of Ohio, cited throughout the record — from public-records law to the economic-development and siting authorities.

nodes.label: PFAS
nodes.desc: A large class of persistent synthetic fluorinated compounds, increasingly regulated in drinking water, effluent, and biosolids.

nodes.label: PILOT
nodes.desc: A negotiated payment that substitutes for the property taxes abated on a development, often directed to specific recipients like a school district.

nodes.label: PJM
nodes.desc: The regional transmission organization that operates the high-voltage grid and wholesale electricity market across Ohio and the mid-Atlantic.

nodes.label: POTW
nodes.desc: The Clean Water Act term for a municipally owned wastewater treatment works — the public peer of a private industrial discharger.

nodes.label: PTI
nodes.desc: Ohio EPA's pre-construction permit for a new or modified source of air or water pollution, issued before ground is broken.

nodes.label: Public-records mandamus
nodes.desc: In Ohio, a writ of mandamus is the remedy that compels a public office to produce records improperly withheld under the Public Records Act.

nodes.label: PUCO
nodes.desc: Ohio's utility regulator, overseeing the rates and service of electric, gas, water, and telecom utilities in the state.

nodes.label: PUE
nodes.desc: A data center's total facility energy divided by its IT-load energy — the standard measure of how much overhead (mostly cooling) its computing carries.

nodes.label: Rezoning
nodes.desc: A legislative change to a parcel's zoning district, frequently the approval that unlocks — or blocks — a large project.

nodes.label: RFP
nodes.desc: A solicitation asking firms to submit a scoped, priced proposal, evaluated on a combination of approach and cost.

nodes.label: RFQ
nodes.desc: A solicitation asking firms to submit their qualifications, used to shortlist or select on competence rather than price.

nodes.label: Roadwork Development Agreement
nodes.desc: The agreement under which the developer funds the public road work around the campus — a ~$14.5M "Company Contribution" set against the $14.2M cost estimate, with clauses on grant-refunds, records-notice, and procurement.

nodes.label: RSEI
nodes.desc: EPA's model that converts Toxics Release Inventory reports into a comparative, toxicity- and exposure-weighted chronic-risk score.

nodes.label: RTO
nodes.desc: The independent operator that runs the transmission grid and wholesale energy market for a multi-state region — PJM in this record.

nodes.label: SNC
nodes.desc: EPA's flag for a permittee whose violations are serious or chronic enough to warrant a formal enforcement response.

nodes.label: SOS
nodes.desc: The state office that holds business-entity filings — the public trail from an LLC back toward the people and companies behind it.

nodes.label: SSA
nodes.desc: An EPA designation for an aquifer that supplies most of the drinking water for an area with no readily available alternative source.

nodes.label: SWAT
nodes.desc: A watershed-scale model that simulates runoff, sediment, and nutrient loading across a basin to support TMDL and land-use analysis.

nodes.label: SWCD
nodes.desc: A local district that administers soil, drainage, and stormwater conservation programs, often reviewing the erosion controls on new development.

nodes.label: Tax abatement
nodes.desc: A negotiated reduction or exemption of property taxes granted to attract or retain development — the umbrella over Ohio's CRA, enterprise-zone, and TIF tools.

nodes.label: TIF
nodes.desc: A financing tool that earmarks the property-tax increment from new development to pay for public infrastructure serving it.

nodes.label: TMDL
nodes.desc: The maximum pollutant load an impaired water body can receive and still meet water-quality standards, apportioned among the sources that contribute it.

nodes.label: Total nitrogen
nodes.desc: A nutrient water-quality parameter summing the nitrogen species in a sample, tracked alongside phosphorus in loading and TMDL analysis.

nodes.label: Total phosphorus
nodes.desc: A nutrient water-quality parameter measuring all forms of phosphorus in a sample; excess loading drives the Lake Erie / Maumee algal-bloom problem.

nodes.label: TRI
nodes.desc: EPA's annual, facility-level inventory of reported toxic-chemical releases to air, water, and land — the data behind the RSEI risk model.

nodes.label: USGS
nodes.desc: The federal science agency that operates the national streamgage network and publishes the water, terrain, and geology data the analysis rests on.

nodes.label: Variance
nodes.desc: A parcel-specific waiver of a zoning standard granted by a board of zoning appeals when strict application would impose an undue hardship.

nodes.label: WLA
nodes.desc: The share of a TMDL assigned to point-source dischargers, translated into the effluent limits of their NPDES permits.

nodes.label: WUE
nodes.desc: A data center's water use per unit of IT energy — the cooling-water efficiency ratio; whether it counts withdrawal or consumption depends on how it is reported, so the basis has to be recorded before the number is used.

nodes.label: WWTP
nodes.desc: The plant that treats sewage and industrial wastewater before discharging treated effluent to a receiving water under an NPDES permit.
